bbva-open-deal-room.title: Nirium at The Open Deal Room by Stellar — BBVA Tower, Mexico City
bbva-open-deal-room.excerpt: We were one of six Stellar startups featured at La Arena inside BBVA Tower CDMX. Here is what we showed, who was in the room, and why an autonomous treasury agent belongs in front of institutional investors.
bbva-open-deal-room.h1: Nirium at The Open Deal Room by Stellar
bbva-open-deal-room.p1: On May 21, 2026, Nirium was featured at The Open Deal Room by Stellar, hosted inside BBVA Tower in Mexico City. We were one of six Stellar ecosystem startups invited to La Arena — a curated room where builders present in front of venture investors, angels, and institutional players active in the Mexican fintech landscape.
bbva-open-deal-room.p2: It is not every day that an autonomous, on-chain treasury agent gets to stand in the lobby of one of Latin America's largest banks. That contrast is exactly the point.
bbva-open-deal-room.pitch_hook_quote: As a founder, I was my own treasurer — and I slept. So did the money.
bbva-open-deal-room.pitch_problem: We opened with a problem every Mexican founder feels: corporate cash sits idle. It loses roughly 10% a year to inflation while it sleeps in an account, and keeping it productive is a 24/7 manual job nobody has time for.
bbva-open-deal-room.pitch_solution: Then the turn — Nirium wakes the money that sleeps. An autonomous agent moves idle USDC into CETES, Mexican sovereign debt, through Etherfuse, and back to liquid the moment it is needed: instantly, and without a treasury desk.
bbva-open-deal-room.pitch_team: We closed on the team: Giovanny Amador (Founder) and Monserrat Mendoza (Co-founder) — the same duo that placed 3rd at the Fintech World Cup México with a previous project. A team that has already shipped and won together.
bbva-open-deal-room.presented_p1: We walked the room through the core of Nirium: a non-custodial agent that moves idle corporate USDC into Mexican government bonds (CETES) through Etherfuse, 24/7, with a Soroban contract enforcing every transfer.
bbva-open-deal-room.presented_p2: The message we kept returning to is the security pattern that makes this safe to put in front of institutions. An AI agent can read the market and propose a rebalance, but it never holds custody — a 2-of-3 Soroban multisig vault enforces delegation scopes on-chain, so a compromised or hallucinating agent physically cannot move funds the contract did not authorize.
bbva-open-deal-room.pattern_quote: The LLM proposes, the contract decides.
bbva-open-deal-room.venue_p1: Tokenized real-world assets in Mexico are no longer a thesis on a slide. CETES on Stellar via a regulated operator is a live corridor, and seeing it discussed inside BBVA Tower — rather than a hackathon side room — signals how quickly institutional appetite is forming. Nirium's position is deliberately software-only and non-custodial: regulated partners handle settlement, while we provide the rails developers and fintechs embed.
bbva-open-deal-room.takeaway_p1: Beyond the pitch, the value of La Arena was the conversations it opened — with investors and ecosystem operators who understand both the Stellar stack and the Mexican regulatory context. Those are the relationships that turn a working testnet protocol into a funded, audited, mainnet product. We left with new threads to pull, and a clearer read on what institutional partners need to see next: verifiable adoption, not promises.
bbva-open-deal-room.where_body: Nirium runs live on Stellar testnet — an autonomous agent, published TypeScript and Python SDKs, native x402/MPP agentic payments, and an immutable audit trail. Mainnet remains audit-gated. Backed by the Stellar ecosystem: SCF Kickstart grant, SDF Scale graduate, and an active Stellar Mexico Ambassador.

nature.title: 1. Nature of Service and Regulatory Framework
nature.content: Nirium is exclusively technology infrastructure software (IaaS). Nirium operates strictly as a B2B software provider facilitating treasury flow orchestration and is NOT a Financial Technology Institution (ITF), IFPE, or banking entity, and does not perform regulated financial activity. The platform provides immutable forensic telemetry and Soroban protocols. Custody, settlement, and issuance services for any real-world asset are the exclusive responsibility of regulated third-party providers (e.g., Etherfuse) under their own licenses and terms of service. Nirium never holds client funds.

no_guarantees.title: 2. No Guarantees — Service Level Agreement (SLA)
no_guarantees.content:
Nirium does not guarantee financial returns of any kind nor assumes responsibility for secondary market liquidity. Routing projections and spread metrics are strictly informational and reflect historical algorithmic execution on Stellar Testnet.

Nirium is not an investment product, security, or mutual fund. Capital remains under the sovereign control of the regulated operator's corporate keys at all times. Nirium is an automation SDK with which institutions interact assuming the technological risk.

ai_liability.title: 3. Autonomous Node & Oracle Liability
ai_liability.content: By activating infrastructure nodes or approval logic, the institution grants a technical mandate for the code to propose transactions based on pre-configured corporate thresholds. The operator acknowledges that automated systems, price oracles, and external APIs may exhibit critical latency, service outages, or corrupt data. Nirium acts as a middleware layer and assumes no liability for losses derived from systemic failures in the underlying settlement rails or the public Stellar network.

rwa_disclaimer.title: 4. Sovereign Asset (CETES) Risks
rwa_disclaimer.content: Operations with CETES are subject to institutional availability, banking window constraints, and Banxico regulations. Nirium acts solely as a technological bridge (Middleware) and, where autonomous rebalancing is enabled, holds only the RebalanceManager role on a client-owned DeFindex vault — a role that cannot withdraw funds. Counterparty risk, legal custody of the underlying asset, and AML compliance rest entirely with the bond issuer, the final custodian, and the regulated operator. CETES exposure occurs on Stellar Mainnet through client-owned, third-party-audited vaults (invite-only pending legal review) and, separately, as a Stellar Testnet proof of concept via Nirium's own NiriumVault contract.

dispute.content: Any controversy related to software licensing shall be resolved through binding arbitration under the rules of the Mexico City Chamber of Commerce. By provisioning a corporate environment, the institution expressly waives class-action lawsuits. These terms are governed by the federal laws of the United Mexican States.

infrastructure.title: 6. Infrastructure Availability (SaaS)
infrastructure.content: Nirium provides software services on an 'as is' basis. As final execution depends on the Stellar network and third-party APIs (e.g., Etherfuse), Nirium does not guarantee a 100% availability SLA. The platform implements cryptographic security protocols, but is not liable for losses resulting from blockchain congestion, network forks, or outages of third-party cloud services (AWS/GCP).

reverse_solicitation.content: Nirium does not make a public offering of securities, payment intermediation, or retail financial services. Access by foreign corporations is a private B2B request. restricted_jurisdictions.title: 8. Restricted Jurisdictions and Sanctions
restricted_jurisdictions.content: Nirium is established in Mexico and does not offer its services into jurisdictions where those services would constitute regulated activity, regardless of how the software is built. Access is prohibited from comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions, jurisdictions subject to a Financial Action Task Force call for action, and mainland China. compliance.title: Compliance & Institutional Trust
compliance.disclosure_text: Nirium is strictly a software and infrastructure provider (SDK/API). We do not operate as a Financial Technology Institution (ITF), do not manage third-party funds, and are not subject to registration under Art. 80 of the Fintech Law. All operational, KYC, AML, and compliance responsibilities fall entirely on the regulated institutional operator utilizing our infrastructure. Nirium acts solely as a decentralized routing layer on Soroban.
compliance.non_custodial_manifesto: The non-custodial nature of Nirium's infrastructure ensures that the institution or operator maintains exclusive control over their private keys and treasury assets at all times. Our execution nodes operate strictly under predefined, auditable smart contract (Soroban) authorizations.
compliance.atomic_proof: Every automated action is backed by an atomic on-chain proof. You can audit any transaction executed by the SDK through the Stellar block explorer (Stellar.Expert).
compliance.scf_conduct: Utilization of this SDK implies strict adherence to the Stellar Code of Conduct (May 2026) and the responsible innovation principles of the ecosystem (Stellar ecosystem).

legal.disclaimer_short: Nirium is experimental software on Stellar Testnet. Not financial advice. No yields, dividends, or returns guaranteed. Use at your own risk.
legal.disclaimer_full: Nirium is software-only, non-custodial infrastructure and never holds client funds. Non-custodial settlement (x402/MPP), audit anchoring and reporting run on Stellar mainnet; the autonomous treasury vault runs on Stellar testnet, audit-gated, until a formal external audit. Nirium is not financial advice, not an investment product, and not a regulated financial activity. It does not guarantee yields, dividends, asset appreciation, or returns of any kind. Reference rate data displayed (e.g., Etherfuse CETES) is public reference information only — not projections or promises of return. XLM and Stellar assets are volatile. Financial services are provided by regulated partners, not by Nirium.
